title: In-the-money call spread versus out-of-the-money put spread
summary: An in-the-money debit call spread and an out-of-the-money put credit spread at the same strikes are the same trade by put-call parity. Many traders pick the put spread because its bid-ask spread is tighter. The speaker works a limit order just above the mid on the call spread and often gets a better fill than he would on the put spread.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $110. Both spreads use the $95 and $100 strikes, below the market.
The in-the-money debit call spread: buy the 95 call, sell the 100 call.
The out-of-the-money put credit spread: sell the 100 put, buy the 95 put. Same shape.
The difference is about zero: put-call parity makes them the same trade. What differs is the fill.
Both break even at the same price. A better fill moves the breakeven in your favor.

takeaways: An ITM debit call spread equals an OTM put credit spread at the same strikes.
A tighter bid-ask spread on the put side does not mean a better trade.
Work a limit order near the mid on the call spread; fills are often better than the quote suggests.
caveats: Part of the transcript is missing. Fill quality varies by stock and market; the speaker's experience is not verified data.
